Subject: POC: Redwood integration plan & success criteria

Hi Alice / Bob

Great to chat today. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the 3-week POC:

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for Acme's in-product assistant: latency < 250ms median, cost <= $0.002 / 1k tokens, and accuracy on our top-10 prompts >= 90% match to baseline responses.
- Scope: generation + streaming for live UI, embeddings for search/rerank in a follow-on task, and one tool-calling webhook for order lookup.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: median end-to-end < 250ms for 512-token context under 95th percentile traffic in staging.
2) Quality: pass 8/10 evaluation prompts with parity to your existing assistant (or better).
3) Stability: no more than 2 errors/hour during a 2-hour soak test.
4) Integration: working streaming responses to your UI + one tool call flow + documented SDK integration.

POC timeline (tentative):
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff, grant test API keys, share security questionnaire, agree on test dataset.
- Week 1: SDK integration + sample calls, streaming enabled, basic telemetry.
- Week 2: Load soak, quality evaluation, iterate on prompts & model config.
- Week 3: Final report, go/no-go decision and recommendations.

Owners:
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (PM lead), Dev Patel (integration engineer).
- Acme: Alice Johnson (product), Bob Lee (engineering).

Attachments: draft POC plan + integration checklist attached.

Ask: can you confirm the success criteria above and whether the 3-week timeline works? Also please confirm whether you need VPC/private deployment for the POC or if hosted API is acceptable for the trial.

Thanks,
Marissa

thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Success criteria: the latency target is great; for cost we'll evaluate total cost-of-inference over a 7-day synthetic run, not just per-token. Can you include an estimate of expected spend for a 7-day soak at our baseline traffic?
- Data residency: for the POC we prefer hosted API but we need to ensure logs and telemetry are stored in the US only. Is that doable?
- Streaming & tool calling: streaming is required. For the tool call, we need idempotency guarantees for order lookups; can you confirm Redwood will surface request IDs or allow us to pass our own?
- Evaluation: we'll provide the top-10 prompts and expected canonical answers. Can you confirm how you'll score fuzzy matches?
- Security: attaching our security questions doc — can someone from your security team respond within 3 business days?

Timeline: the 3-week plan looks fine, but we'll need a kickoff next Monday (29 Mar) to get internal approvals.

Thanks — copying Bob for engineering confirmation.

Thanks Alice — answers inline below and an updated POC plan attached.

- Cost estimate: we'll model expected spend for a 7-day soak at your baseline traffic — Dev will run numbers once we have the token profile. Expect a draft estimate by EOD tomorrow.
- Data residency: hosted API with US-only telemetry storage is supported for POC. We'll add a clause in the trial agreement to restrict log egress to US regions.
- Idempotency for tool calls: Redwood supports passing a client-supplied request_id header; we can also return an internal request_id for tracing. That will satisfy order lookup idempotency.
- Scoring: we use a hybrid approach: exact match first, then fuzzy similarity (token-level BLEU + embedding cosine with a threshold). We'll provide the scoring script and thresholds so you can reproduce results.

Updated POC plan (high level):
Phase A (Week 0-1): Kickoff + SDK integration
- Provide API key, sample app, and example code for Python/Node SDKs.
- Integrate streaming endpoint to your UI (ws/HTTP chunked).
Phase B (Week 1-2): Feature validation
- Implement tool-calling webhook + idempotency.
- Run initial eval on your top-10 prompts; iterate on prompt templates and model config.
Phase C (Week 2-3): Soak & report
- 48-hour soak at staging traffic levels + 2-hour high-load soak.
- Deliver final metrics, cost breakdown, and recommended configuration.

Owners:
- Redwood: Marissa (PM), Dev (integration lead) will be primary points of contact.
- Acme: Alice (PM), Bob (Eng) — please confirm Bob will own infra changes.

Kickoff: Mar 29 at 10am PT proposed. Does that work?

I've attached the updated POC plan and the integration checklist. We'll also circulate the scoring notebook and cost model after Dev runs the token profile.

Cheers,
Marissa

Forwarding implementation notes below — tagging Bob for any infra-specific questions.

Implementation notes (technical):
1) SDKs: we provide Python and Node SDKs. Quickstart: pip install redwood-inference / npm i @redwood/inference.

2) API routes:
- POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate (sync generation)
- POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream (server-sent events / websocket for streaming)
- POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/function_call (tool-calling endpoint)

3) Streaming: we support SSE and websocket. Example (curl SSE):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -N 
    -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-1","input":"Hello"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/stream

4) Tool calling: define a function schema in your call payload. We'll return a function_call object with arguments and a request_id header; your webhook should respond with 200 and idempotency_key handling.

5) Auth & env: set REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENV=staging, REDWOOD_REGION=us. We'll create a scoped key with limited TTL for the POC.

6) Telemetry: include x-request-id on all calls. We'll ingest request_id and map to our traces; please also send client_time to help us correlate.

7) Rate limits & batching: POC keys will have burst limits; for steady-state tests we'll provide a recommended batching policy (Dev will send config).

8) Example Node snippet (high level):
  const rw = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new rw.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  const stream = client.stream({ model: 'rw-chat-1', input: 'Hi' });
  stream.on('data', chunk => console.log(chunk));

Next steps for us: we need a test API key, a small test dataset (your top-10 prompts + labels), and confirmation whether your UI prefers SSE or websocket for streaming.

Happy to join Monday's kickoff — I'll set a calendar hold once we confirm time.

Thanks,
